# awscc_lambda_network_connector (Data Source)

Data Source schema for AWS::Lambda::NetworkConnector



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network connector.
- `configuration` (Attributes) The network configuration for the connector. Specify a VpcEgressConfiguration to enable outbound traffic routing through your VPC. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration))
- `latest_version` (Number) The version number of the network connector's latest version. Updates to the connector's configuration create a new immutable version; this attribute exposes the most recent one.
- `latest_version_arn` (String) The qualified Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network connector's latest version. Includes the immutable version suffix and can be used to pin to a specific version.
- `name` (String) A unique name for the network connector within your account and Region. Must be 1 to 64 alphanumeric characters, hyphens, or underscores.
- `operator_role` (String) The ARN of the IAM role that Lambda assumes to manage elastic network interfaces in your VPC. This role must have permissions for ec2:CreateNetworkInterface and related describe operations.
- `state` (String) The current state of the network connector.
- `tags` (Attributes Set) A list of tags to apply to the network connector. Use tags to categorize network connectors for cost allocation, access control, or operational management. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration`

Read-Only:

- `vpc_egress_configuration` (Attributes) The VPC egress configuration for the network connector. Specifies the subnets, security groups, and network protocol for routing outbound traffic through your VPC. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--vpc_egress_configuration))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--vpc_egress_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.vpc_egress_configuration`

Read-Only:

- `associated_compute_resource_types` (List of String) The types of Lambda compute resources that can use this connector. Supported values are MicroVm and WebFunction.
- `elastic_ip_configuration` (Attributes) Specifies whether Lambda assigns an Elastic IP address to each of the network connector's elastic network interfaces (ENIs). If you don't specify an Elastic IP configuration, no Elastic IP address is assigned. When you update this configuration, the change applies to the ENIs of the new connector version. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--vpc_egress_configuration--elastic_ip_configuration))
- `network_protocol` (String) The network protocol for the connector. Specify IPv4 for IPv4-only networking, or DualStack for both IPv4 and IPv6.
- `security_group_ids` (List of String) The IDs of the VPC security groups to attach to the ENIs. All security groups must be in the same VPC as the subnets.
- `subnet_ids` (List of String) The IDs of the VPC subnets where Lambda provisions elastic network interfaces (ENIs). Specify 1 to 16 subnets. All subnets must be in the same VPC.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--vpc_egress_configuration--elastic_ip_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.vpc_egress_configuration.elastic_ip_configuration`

Read-Only:

- `type` (String) The Elastic IP address type for the connector's ENIs. With None, Lambda doesn't assign an Elastic IP address. With ServiceManaged, Lambda allocates a service-managed Elastic IP address in your account for each ENI, associates it with that ENI, and releases it when it deletes the ENI. The connector's operator role must allow the ec2:AllocateAddress and ec2:AssociateAddress actions on Elastic IP addresses and on the connector's ENIs.




<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Read-Only:

- `key` (String) The key name of the tag.
- `value` (String) The value for the tag.
